title: Improve page load performance
when: A web page loads slowly, shows content late, shifts while loading, or the user asks to make the site faster.
inputs: the HTML, CSS, scripts and images
prompt:
Goal: The main content renders fast with no layout shift, and nothing render blocking or oversized is left on the first view.
Steps:
1. Inventory what loads: count files and sizes of images, scripts, styles and fonts; the biggest items come first.
2. Resize and compress images to their displayed size, give each width and height, and add loading="lazy" to images below the first screen.
3. Make scripts non blocking: defer or type="module" in the head, and remove unused libraries.
4. Keep CSS small and in one file; inline only a few lines of critical CSS if the page is tiny.
5. Fonts: at most two families and weights, font-display: swap, and preload only the main one.
6. Defer work not needed at start (charts, maps, heavy widgets) until visible or on interaction.
Quality bar:
- The hero text appears without waiting for scripts.
- No layout shift from images or fonts.
- Total first load is as small as the content allows.
Pitfalls:
- Lazy loading the main hero image.
- Huge background images used as decoration.
- Loading the same script twice.
Verify:
- [ ] Scripts in the head use defer or module.
- [ ] Images have width and height.
- [ ] Images after the first are lazy.
- [ ] Scripts parse.
Output: Updated HTML, CSS and assets plus a short list of what was reduced and by how much.

examples.input: meu site demora muito pra abrir
examples.output: 4 MB of photos resized to 180 KB, scripts deferred, fonts cut to one family with swap
